data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's mechanism never establishes the causal link the problem demands for separating genuine gain from mere compliance. It states the checklist 'distills expert heuristics into verifiable procedural steps' and 'reduces variance,' but if the steps are merely a distillation of the expert's own heuristics, then panel success on the divergence stratum could be caused by the distillation correcting a sporadic expert error (a genuine reliability gain) OR by the panel mechanically applying a rule that happens to match the ground truth on those cases without any underlying epistemic leverage (mere compliance). SRC_002 asserts the divergence stratum 'isolates the causal contribution,' but isolation requires ruling out the confound stated in its own third countercondition: that compliance correlates with correctness because the checklist is a difficulty proxy. Its mechanism provides no causal story for why adherence to verifiable rules — as opposed to the rules tracking an environmental regularity independent of the panel's reasoning — is the operative cause. Without that, the distinguishing evidence it cites is consistent with the very mere-compliance explanation it is supposed to rule out.
